device.name: KDS Gemini 88 Plus dual-rate syringe pump

facts.text: The repository controls a KDS Gemini 88 dual-rate syringe pump from Python over a serial COM port
The pump can infuse with one syringe and withdraw with the other, at different rates
The upstream's example command is 'condition Independent'
In the independent condition the commands take channel a, b or ab
The tutorial lists the command forms for syringe selection, syringe volume, diameter, target time, target volume, infusion rate, run, status and stop
The example syringe selection is 'syr ab sst 1'
'status' reports the state of the pumps
A command is written as its bytes plus a carriage return and a line feed
The serial port defaults to 9600 baud, a 10 s timeout, odd parity, two stop bits and seven data bits
The upstream reads the reply bytes waiting on the port
The example sends the command through realSerial.writeSerial and optionally reads the reply through realSerial.readSerial
The README says the pump stops when it reaches the volume specified in the code
The README says the pump's display need not change when software controls it
The README names pyserial 3.5 as the serial dependency
